text: {"observations": "Image 1 shows several harmonic vocalisations: about 0.4-1.8 s, a long one from about 3.3-6.8 s, and a weaker one from about 7.2-9.8 s. Energy reaches up to about 3.5-4 kHz, with breathy or noisy segments mixed in. In Image 2 (0-2 kHz), the harmonics around 4.4 s sit near 420, 830, 1270 and 1680 Hz, so the fundamental is about 400 Hz. Pitch rises and falls, then glides down to about 200 Hz over several seconds, and the voice has a nasal, wavering quality. These drawn-out, pitch-contoured, noisy-harmonic calls fit a cat meow or yowl. A cow moo would have a much lower fundamental (about 100-150 Hz), which rules out D. Dog barks are short and broadband, which rules out B. Bird calls are typically higher-pitched and faster, which rules out C. The evidence points to A, cat.", "answer": "A"}
